# Agent Skills



This repository contains [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/home) for Google
products and technologies, including [Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com).

## Installation

```bash
npx skills add google/skills
```

When prompted, select specific skills or all skills, the target agents to
configure, and the installation scope (project or global).

If `npx` is not available in your environment, install
[Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download), which includes `npm` and `npx`.

## Updating Skills

To update previously installed skills to the latest versions, run the following
command.

```bash
npx skills update
```

This command gives you an option to also remove obsolete skills.

Plugins

This repo also bundles Google product plugins (Skills + MCP servers) for agent harnesses.

Agent harness Install
Claude Code claude plugin marketplace add google/skills, then claude plugin install <plugin>@google-plugins
Codex codex plugin marketplace add google/skills, then install from the /plugins browser
Antigravity CLI agy plugin install https://github.com/google/skills/<plugin-path>

Support

If you need help or encounter issues with these skills, search for existing issues or open a new one in the GitHub Issue Tracker.

Contributing

We welcome contributions to improve our skills. You can help by:

  • Reporting bugs or inaccuracies in the skill Markdown files.
  • Suggesting new skills to add to this repository (for example, Google technologies or recipes) by filing a feature request.

License

You are free to copy, modify, and distribute these skills under the terms of the Apache 2.0 license. See the LICENSE file for details.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A collection of reusable, composable skills for building advanced conversational AI agents for Google products.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This repository provides a standardized library of modular 'skills' designed to be integrated into conversational AI systems and autonomous agents, specifically tailored for Google products and technologies. Developed by Google, it aims to create a common interface for tasks across Google Cloud, AI/ML platforms, infrastructure, databases, and developer tools, allowing developers to plug and play these capabilities. The framework emphasizes composability, enabling complex behaviors to be constructed by chaining multiple fundamental skills together. It is built to be agnostic of the underlying LLM, focusing heavily on the execution and parameterization of the tasks.
keyFeatures: Standardized interfaces: Defines a consistent contract for inputs and outputs across all provided skills for seamless integration.
Modular design: Allows developers to import only the specific capabilities they need without pulling in a monolithic framework.
Google Cloud integration: Provides extensive pre-built skills for managing GKE, BigQuery, Cloud SQL, and other Google Cloud services.
Skill composition: Enables the chaining of multiple basic skills to perform complex, multi-step operations efficiently.
Cross-harness compatibility: Includes plugins and MCP servers compatible with Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity CLI.

useCases.title: Virtual assistant development
useCases.description: Developers build custom conversational agents that can check analytics, manage cloud infrastructure, and query databases using these modular components.

useCases.title: Enterprise automation
useCases.description: Teams integrate specific skills into their internal chat bots to allow employees to automatically configure GKE clusters or generate monitoring charts.

useCases.title: Cross-platform agents
useCases.description: Engineers use the standardized interfaces to ensure their agent's tools work consistently regardless of which LLM is powering the underlying reasoning.

useCases.title: Cloud infrastructure management
useCases.description: DevOps professionals utilize pre-built skills to automate deployment workflows, perform cost optimization analysis, and troubleshoot workloads.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: AI developers and software engineers building conversational interfaces or autonomous agents, particularly those working extensively within the Google Cloud ecosystem. It helps architects plug capabilities directly into existing applications to rapidly scale operations.
